tools.name: run_student_safety_checklist
tools.description: Run the Student Protection Readiness Checklist. Accepts a parent/guardian's answers to the 12 readiness questions (q1-q12, each an integer 1-4) and returns a normalized readiness score (0-100), a score band/category, the top protection gaps (key findings), a plain-language interpretation, per-category scores, and a recommended next step. This is decision support only — it does not diagnose bullying, abuse, or mental health conditions and does not replace emergency services or professionals.

answers.description: Answers to the 12 readiness questions. Keys are q1 through q12, values are integers 1 (lowest readiness) to 4 (highest readiness). Categories: Warning Sign Awareness (q1,q3,q5,q6), Communication Safety (q2,q11), Documentation Readiness (q4), School Escalation Readiness (q7,q8), Response Confidence (q9,q10,q12).

q1.description: [warning_signs] How confident are you that you could recognize early changes in your child's mood, behavior, or social patterns?

q2.description: [communication] If something was bothering your child at school, how likely is it they would tell you about it?

q3.description: [warning_signs] How well do you understand the difference between normal social conflict and patterns that may require attention?

q4.description: [documentation] If a concern started to develop, would you know what to document and how to track it?

q5.description: [warning_signs] How often do you check in with your child about their social experiences at school?

q6.description: [warning_signs] Would you notice if your child started avoiding certain activities, people, or places?

q7.description: [escalation] Do you know when it would be appropriate to involve the school in a concern about your child?

q8.description: [escalation] Do you know who to contact at your child's school if you needed to raise a concern?

q9.description: [response] If you confirmed something concerning was happening, how confident are you in knowing what to do next?

q10.description: [response] Do you feel you could stay calm and structured if your child disclosed something upsetting?

q11.description: [communication] Does your child have other trusted adults they could talk to if they were not comfortable coming to you?

q12.description: [response] Overall, how prepared do you feel to protect your child if a situation was developing at school?
